newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Soros sees Euro single currency on time.
newsitem.headline: Soros sees Euro single currency on time.

text.p: Financial investor George Soros said he believed the European single currency would be launched on time and said a delay past the planned 1999 start would be catastrophic.
"We are going to have it on January 1, 1999," Soros told reporters, referring to the scheduled launch date of the single currency under Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"I believe the political decision has been made (to go ahead)," he added at a news conference at the World Economic Forum.
"A delay would be catastrophic," he said without elaborating.
But Soros, who refused to answer any questions about his investment strategy, said that the EMU project was flawed.
He noted that the labour market in many European countries was too rigid.

Strict budget criteria for entry to the single currency would prevent governments from taking action to cut the employee taxes companies have to pay and which were a key factor in the high level of unemployment in many parts of western Europe, he said.
"Tax reductions would temporarily increase the deficit but would reduce unemployment," he said. This decline in the jobless levels would in turn eventually help cut budget deficits, he said.
